claims.text: An ML workflow correlating alloy composition, processing parameters, and microstructure can identify new HEA processing routes that concurrently improve strength and ductility.
The proposed ML-guided routes can increase yield strength by at least 10–20% while maintaining or improving ductility above 10%.
HEAs often face a trade-off between high strength and high ductility.
As-cast or partially processed HEAs often have limited ductility.
A model trained on composition, microstructure, processing, and mechanical-property data can recommend novel heat-treatment and deformation schedules.
ML-guided processing will produce fine-scale lamellar or precipitate-rich microstructures.
Fine lamellar microstructures can provide a combination of high strength and high ductility in HEAs.
Fine lamellar or precipitate-rich microstructures enable balanced strain hardening and controlled dislocation slip.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitates relieve stress concentrations that would otherwise promote premature crack initiation.
Dual-phase regions inhibit crack initiation while sustaining dislocation activity.
Coherent nanoprecipitation can produce ultrahigh strength together with tensile ductility above 10% in a refractory HEA.
The ML-guided route will achieve yield strength of at least 2 GPa or at least 10–20% above baseline.
The ML-guided route will preserve or increase tensile ductility beyond 10%.
Some HEAs can attain approximately 2 GPa strength while retaining more than 10% tensile ductility.
Typical equiatomic HEAs reach approximately 2 GPa strength but often exhibit less than 10% elongation.
Coarse or brittle phases are responsible for the limited ductility of typical equiatomic HEAs.
The ML model requires sufficiently diverse and accurate composition and processing data.
Extrapolation outside well-characterized composition ranges risks ML prediction errors.
Direct experimental validation of the proposed ML approach is limited, so its generalizability and predictive power remain uncertain.
